solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One with access to select info on crew ignoring energy of No. 8 in the past

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so a letter is dropped from the word

blocks.clueFragment: One with access to select info
blocks.note: someone privy to restricted information
a rowing crew of eight oarsmen is called an eight
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A crew member with privileged access to information, written off as an old figure from the past.
explanation.walkthrough: A rowing crew of eight is itself called an eight. In old football formations the inside right wore the number 8 shirt, before modern positions replaced the term.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically the forward playing between centre forward and outside right wore shirt number eight in a football lineup.

clue.text: Metamorphosis of an insect for example

indicators.note: a metamorphosis is a complete change of form, so the letters take a new shape

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A caterpillar turning into a butterfly, offered as a textbook case of transformation.
explanation.walkthrough: Metamorphosis is apt for an insect, which is why it reads as biology rather than an instruction to rearrange letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'for instance' is interchangeable with 'for example', so the word on its own stands for an illustrative case.

clue.text: Almost certain to rise and overcome

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: certain means sure
to mount is to go up or climb

explanation.surface: Someone nearly sure to climb up and beat their difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims only the word right after it, not the whole clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To overcome an obstacle is to get on top of it, which is exactly the verb's sense of conquering difficulty.

clue.text: Mythological princess removed from model of scene in play

indicators.note: something removed from a word is taken out of it, leaving the rest

blocks.note: a diorama is a three-dimensional model of a scene
Io was a princess in Greek myth, loved by Zeus and turned into a heifer

explanation.surface: A figure from legend dropped out of a stage set's scale model.
explanation.walkthrough: IO comes out of DIORAMA. Io is the crossword's favourite mythological princess because her name is so short.
explanation.definitionFit: A play is a theatrical work, and drama is the general word for such stage works.

clue.text: Uproar caused by technique of literary analysis? Not half

indicators.note: not half means half is missing, so the first part of the word is discarded

blocks.note: deconstruction is Derrida's method of critical reading

explanation.surface: Academic outrage stirred up by a fashionable theory of reading texts.
explanation.walkthrough: DECONSTRUCTION has fourteen letters; dropping the first seven leaves the answer. 'Not half' is also British slang for 'very much', which disguises it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruction is a noisy disturbance or quarrel, a close synonym of commotion and row.

clue.text: Beginning with information on European ship carrying ivory primarily

indicators.note: a vessel carrying cargo has it inside, so one piece goes within another
primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is used

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
E is the abbreviation for European
SS stands for steamship
first letter of ivory

explanation.surface: Starting out with a briefing about a European vessel transporting ivory.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for information. In a down clue 'on' puts a piece above the next, and the ship carries the ivory's first letter in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis means origin or creation, the first book of the Bible being named for the world's beginning.

clue.text: Way of handling soldiers and volunteers upset by months under canvas

indicators.note: to upset is to tip over, and in a down clue that turns a piece upside down
being under canvas means being inside a shelter, so these pieces sit within another

blocks.note: the Royal Engineers
the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
M is an abbreviation for month
a tent is made of canvas

explanation.surface: How troops and reservists are dealt with after months camping in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: RE plus TA turned over plus M go inside TENT. The surface suggests army camp life, which hides the abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment is the manner in which someone or something is dealt with or managed.

clue.text: Money Henry lost in club

indicators.note: something lost is gone, so one letter goes missing from the word

blocks.note: the baht is the currency of Thailand
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A man called Henry losing cash at a gambling club.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry looks like a person, but it is the unit of inductance, symbol H, taken out of BAHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bat, as in cricket or baseball, is a club used to hit the ball.

clue.text: Plot to strike causing pandemonium

blocks.note: a garden plot or flower bed
to lam is to beat or thrash

explanation.surface: A conspiracy to call a walkout that creates chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: Plot suggests a conspiracy and strike a walkout; here they are a garden bed and an old verb for hitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedlam, from the old London asylum Bethlehem Hospital, has come to mean wild uproar and confusion.

clue.text: Despot’s extremely tetchy tirade

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of a word, meaning its two end letters

blocks.note: first and last letters of tetchy
a tirade is a long angry rant

explanation.surface: A dictator delivering a very irritable harangue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for tetchy, but it asks for the word's end letters. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is a ruler with absolute and often cruel power, the same as a tyrant.

clue.text: Songs about arresting tenor found with flutes

definitions.note: plural, while the answer is singular

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the piece is read backwards
arresting someone means holding them, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: airs are tunes or songs
T is the abbreviation for tenor

explanation.surface: Songs featuring a captured tenor, accompanied by flute music.
explanation.walkthrough: AIRS is turned round and T goes inside. Flutes look like musical instruments next to songs and tenor, but they are grooves.
explanation.definitionFit: In architecture flutes are grooves on a column, and a stria is one such narrow groove or channel.

clue.text: Competitor’s fiddle requiring gentle handling

blocks.note: to fiddle is to swindle or con
something tender is sore and must be handled gently

explanation.surface: A rival violinist's instrument is delicate and needs careful treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: Fiddle suggests a violin; it is a swindle. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A contender is someone competing for a prize or title, a rival in a contest.

clue.text: Irregularities of style ultimately evident in fake Mona Lisa

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter is taken
a fake is a made-up imitation, so these letters are rearranged into something new

blocks.note: last letter of style
taken as written

explanation.surface: Stylistic oddities that give away a forged copy of Leonardo's portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as art-forgery detection, and fittingly a fake painting would show irregularities.
explanation.definitionFit: Anomalies are things that deviate from what is normal or expected, which is what irregularities are.

clue.text: Aim of Garfunkel? To go back home

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: Art Garfunkel, singing partner of Paul Simon
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: Asking what Art Garfunkel's ambition is, and answering that it is to return home.
explanation.walkthrough: Garfunkel's first name is reversed and followed by IN. 'Aim of Garfunkel' reads as one phrase but splits after 'Aim'.
explanation.definitionFit: To train a gun or camera on something is to point or direct it, so the verb matches aim.

clue.text: Business interest

blocks.note: first meaning: a firm or commercial enterprise
second meaning: something that matters to or involves you

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase, a stake in a company, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names both a commercial firm, as in a going concern, and a matter that engages someone's attention.

clue.text: Censor has spoken about Italy’s leader

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: to censor is to edit out material
oral means spoken
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A censor has commented on the Italian prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italy's leader' looks like a prime minister; Italy gives I and leader is the definition, a British newspaper term.
explanation.definitionFit: In British newspapers a leader is the main opinion article, also called an editorial or leading article.

clue.text: Lose friends he dated? Only some

indicators.note: only some means just a part, so the letters come from within the phrase

blocks.note: letters spanning the end of friends, all of he, and the start of dated

explanation.surface: Wondering whether to drop the friends she used to go out with, but only a few of them.
explanation.walkthrough: The question reads as relationship advice; the letters run across three words.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed is to get rid of or cast off, as in shedding weight or staff, matching lose.

clue.text: Simpler version of Republican teacher’s reading tool sent up by scholarly people

indicators.note: sent up means moved upward, so in a down clue the letters climb in the opposite order

blocks.note: a lite version is a simplified or reduced one
R is the abbreviation for Republican
the Initial Teaching Alphabet, once used to teach children to read

explanation.surface: Academics mocking a dumbed-down reading aid used by a Republican teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent up' suggests mockery but reverses ITA. The Initial Teaching Alphabet was a phonetic alphabet used in British schools in the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: The literati are well-read, educated people, the intellectual class interested in literature.

clue.text: Established model maker’s latest promotional poster seen around market stall previously

indicators.note: the latest is the last, so only the final letter is taken
something seen around another surrounds it, so one piece goes inside
previously means earlier, so this piece comes first in the answer

blocks.note: a stall in a market is a stand
an advertisement
last letter of maker

explanation.surface: A fashion model's most recent poster campaign displayed around a market stall.
explanation.walkthrough: Model suggests a fashion model, but 'Established model' together is the definition, and maker's latest is just one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is an accepted benchmark or exemplar against which others are measured, also used adjectivally for accepted.

clue.text: Periods without motorway restrictions

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is taken away

blocks.note: periods are times
British motorways are numbered M1, M25 and so on

explanation.surface: Stretches of time with no speed limits on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a road with no speed limit, but 'restrictions' is the definition and M comes out of TIMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Ties are bonds or obligations that limit freedom, as in family ties, so they act as constraints.

clue.text: Hesitation after exams on a kind of ornamental pottery

indicators.note: after means following, so the piece before this word is placed second

blocks.note: SATs are standard national tests in English schools
um is a sound of hesitation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pause after tests on the subject of decorative ceramics.
explanation.walkthrough: SATs are national tests taken in English schools. The answer is better known as a small orange, which makes the pottery sense a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Satsuma ware is a cream-coloured Japanese earthenware decorated with gilding and enamels, named after its province of origin.

clue.text: Vigorous supporter of country park’s opening engaged in unrestrained revelry

indicators.note: an opening is the start, so only the initial letter is taken

blocks.note: first letter of park
at means occupied with, as in at work
a riot of fun is wild merrymaking

explanation.surface: A keen backer of a rural park attending its launch party, which turns wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country park' looks like one phrase but splits: country belongs to the definition. 'Engaged in' looks like a container signal but supplies AT.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriot is someone who loves and zealously defends their nation.

clue.text: Especially valued mature bird’s feathers

blocks.note: a plum job is a highly prized one
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: The prized feathers of an adult bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Plum as an adjective means choice or highly desirable, as in a plum job.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the collective noun for the whole coat of quills and down covering a bird's body.

clue.text: Gutsy to carry on hiding friar after time runs out

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it inside, so one piece goes within another
when time runs out it is gone, so its letter is dropped

blocks.note: to ply a trade is to carry it on
Friar Tuck of the Robin Hood legend
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Brave enough to keep sheltering a monk on the run once the clock expires.
explanation.walkthrough: Friar Tuck is the jovial monk in Robin Hood's band; ply means to work steadily at a trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Plucky means showing pluck, courage in difficulty, the same as gutsy or brave.

clue.text: Unprofitable for a powerful financier they say

indicators.note: what they say is spoken, so the word is matched by sound

blocks.note: a press or oil baron is a powerful business magnate

explanation.surface: A business that doesn't pay for a mighty tycoon, so people claim.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words sound the same in most accents.
explanation.definitionFit: Barren means producing nothing, so a barren venture yields no return or gain.

clue.text: Plain Jane’s heart captured by the Italian student earlier

indicators.note: the heart is the centre, so the middle letters are kept
something captured is held, so one piece goes inside another
earlier means coming first, so this piece leads the answer

blocks.note: L for learner
lo is an Italian form of 'the'
middle two letters of Jane

explanation.surface: An ordinary woman named Jane wins the love of an Italian student.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain Jane' reads as one phrase, but Plain is the definition. Italian has two words for 'the', il and lo; here it is the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A llano is a broad grassy plain in South America, especially in Venezuela and Colombia.

clue.text: Right about a French revolutionary working in a club for police officers

indicators.note: about can mean turned around, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: RT is an abbreviation for right
un is French for 'a'
Che Guevara
on means operating

explanation.surface: A right-winger complaining about a French radical working at a police social club.
explanation.walkthrough: A club for police officers sounds like a social venue, but it is the weapon. Che Guevara is the crossword's stock revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: A truncheon is the short stout stick carried as a weapon by British police, a cudgel or baton.

clue.text: Be concerned about daughter’s group of political activists

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: to care is to be concerned
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A parent worried about a daughter's involvement with radical campaigners.
explanation.walkthrough: CARE wraps round D. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadre is a core group of trained, committed members of a revolutionary party or movement.

clue.text: Arising from circular about university’s courses of study

indicators.note: about can mean all over the place, so the letters are scattered and reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Course programmes that come out of a memo sent round a university.
explanation.walkthrough: Circular reads as a memo distributed to staff; here it is just letters, rearranged with U.
explanation.definitionFit: Curricula is the Latin plural of curriculum, the set programme of subjects taught on a course.

clue.text: Not available after help’s withdrawn by goddess of the hunt

indicators.note: something withdrawn is pulled back, so the letters run backwards
after means following, so the piece before this word is placed second

blocks.note: aid is help
NA is the abbreviation for not available

explanation.surface: Assistance is pulled by the deity of hunting, so it's unavailable.
explanation.walkthrough: Withdrawn reads as help being cancelled, but it is the signal to turn the word round. NA is a standard abbreviation seen on forms.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana is the Roman goddess of hunting, the moon and wild animals, equivalent to Greek Artemis.

clue.text: Yearning for money

blocks.note: first meaning: a strong longing or desire
second meaning: the currency of Japan

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as greed, a longing for cash; the two nouns are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an intense longing and Japan's national currency unit.

clue.text: Forget to take Bottom on holiday

indicators.note: in an across clue one thing on another is attached after it, so the first-named piece comes second

blocks.note: leave is time off work
behind is a colloquial word for the buttocks

explanation.surface: Neglecting to pack Bottom, Shakespeare's weaver, for a trip away.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottom looks like the weaver from A Midsummer Night's Dream, but it means the rear end. Leave is the British word for time off work.
explanation.definitionFit: If you leave something behind you fail to bring it with you, the same as forgetting it.
